observations: Photos 0, 1 and 2 show one white games console with a perforated top grille around a large round vent, the slim Xbox One S body style.
Photo 1 shows the front: an Xbox logo at the right end, a horizontal disc slot, a front USB port at the left, so a disc version, not the all-digital one.
Two controllers: a white Xbox One controller with a 3.5mm jack (photo 1) and a blue Xbox Series style controller with a share button (photos 0 and 2).
The white controller and the console top show scuffs and grime; no cracks or broken parts are visible.
No screen, no power cable, no HDMI cable and no game disc or game list is shown in any photo.
No label with model number, serial or storage size is visible.
Every photo carries a dealer watermark 'KINGSPLEN GAMING GADGETS', a trader shop counter setting.

identity.model: Xbox One S (disc version, storage size unknown)
read_from: photo 1 Xbox logo on the console front
photo 0 and photo 2 Xbox logo on both controllers
photos 0 to 2 One S body shape: perforated top with round vent and front disc slot

claims.evidence: Nothing in the photos shows where the console was used.
Photo 1 Xbox logo on the front and the One S body shape in photos 0 to 2; it is the One S variant.
Photos 0, 1 and 2 show two controllers; one is an Xbox One pad, the other an Xbox Series pad. Neither is shown working.
Cosmetically fair with scuffs and dirt in photos 0 and 2; no clip shows it powering on or playing.

claims.claim: Comes with FC26 package and other
claims.evidence: No screen shot of the game library and no disc is shown; digital games may be tied to the seller's account.

risks.risk: Console may not power on, may overheat or may fail to output picture over HDMI.
risks.proof: A clip of the console powering on from the button and reaching the Xbox dashboard on a TV, with the console in the same shot.
risks.if_unproven: as not working, spares or repair value

risks.risk: Disc drive may not read or eject discs.
risks.proof: A clip inserting a game disc, the game showing on screen, then ejecting it.
risks.if_unproven: as a console with a dead disc drive

risks.risk: Storage size unknown (500GB or 1TB), which sets the price.
risks.proof: A screen shot of Settings, System, Storage showing the drive capacity, or the label on the underside.

risks.risk: Controllers may have stick drift, dead buttons or fail to pair.
risks.proof: A clip of each controller connected and moving the cursor on the dashboard, both sticks and the triggers.
risks.if_unproven: as console only, controllers valued at nothing

risks.risk: FC26 and other games may be digital licences on the seller's account that leave with the account, or the console may be account-locked or banned from online.
risks.proof: A screen shot of the game library under a fresh profile after a factory reset, or the FC26 disc in shot.

risks.risk: Power cable and HDMI cable not shown.
risks.proof: A photo of the power cable and HDMI cable beside the console.

proof_requests: A clip of the console powering on and reaching the Xbox dashboard on a TV, both controllers connected and responding.
A screen shot of Settings, System, Storage showing the capacity, or a photo of the underside label.
A clip of a game disc loading and ejecting.
A screen shot of the game library showing FC26, or the FC26 disc in shot, after a factory reset.
A photo of the power and HDMI cables, with a handwritten note with today's date in the same shot.
response.reason: The brand is read from the logos and the body is unmistakably an Xbox One S disc console with two controllers, so it can be priced at its worst case: 500GB, not proven working, no games. A working clip, the storage screen and the game library would raise it.
